subject: Biotechnology
title: Therapeutic Vaccines
description: A micro-lesson that makes Therapeutic Vaccines usable.

hook.text: Most vaccines prevent disease — therapeutic vaccines treat diseases you already have. They retrain your immunity.

buildup.text: Sipuleucel-T treats prostate cancer — patient's own immune cells are exposed to a tumor antigen and reinfused.

discovery.text: Therapeutic hepatitis B vaccines aim to cure chronic infection — awakening exhausted T cells that ignore the virus.

twist.text: The immune system actively suppresses responses to chronic infections — breaking tolerance is the hardest challenge.

climax.text: Alzheimer's vaccines targeting amyloid plaques entered trials — immunotherapy expanding beyond infectious disease.

punchline.text: Not prevention but cure — therapeutic vaccines fight what is already there.

quiz.question: What makes therapeutic vaccines different from preventive vaccines?
options: They use stronger adjuvants than preventive vaccines
They treat existing diseases by reactivating the immune response against them
They prevent diseases from spreading to other people

details.summary: Therapeutic vaccines treat existing diseases rather than preventing them, training the immune system to clear established infections or tumors. Applications include treating chronic hepatitis B, HPV-related cancers, and HIV, marking a fundamental shift in vaccine philosophy.
details.whyItMatters: Therapeutic vaccines could transform chronic infections and cancers into curable conditions by harnessing the immune system against established disease. Success would change millions of lives where current treatments manage but do not cure.
takeaways: Therapeutic vaccines aim to cure rather than prevent existing diseases
They train the immune system to recognize and clear established pathogens or tumors
Chronic hepatitis B and HIV are primary therapeutic vaccine targets

faq.question: How do therapeutic vaccines differ from preventive vaccines?
faq.answer: Preventive vaccines prime naive immune systems before infection. Therapeutic vaccines must overcome active immune evasion by established pathogens or tumors. They need to reprogram existing tolerance or exhaustion, which is fundamentally harder than educating a fresh immune response.

faq.question: Could a therapeutic vaccine cure chronic hepatitis B?
faq.answer: Clinical trials are testing vaccines combined with antivirals to achieve functional cure of chronic hepatitis B, where the virus is permanently controlled without medication. Current antivirals control but rarely cure the infection affecting 300 million people worldwide.
